title: Keratins coordinate tissue spreading by balancing spreading forces with tissue material properties
task: Determine how keratin networks balance tissue spreading forces with mechanical integrity
key_results: Stress-induced keratin maturation increases tissue viscosity by ~2-fold, preventing rupture during zebrafish embryo spreading; keratins required for both EVL mechanical resilience and yolk cell actomyosin-driven pulling forces
comments: The dual mechanosensitive role of keratins is elegant, though the quantitative relationship between stress, maturation rate, and viscosity change could be more precisely characterized.

model_io.model: Vertex model with mechanochemical feedback
In vivo zebrafish EVL expansion assay

hypotheses.hypothesis: Keratin network maturation is stress-responsive and increases tissue viscosity to prevent rupture
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; genetic interference and rheology experiments demonstrate stress-induced maturation drives viscosity increase

hypotheses.hypothesis: Keratins are required in yolk cell for mechanosensitive force generation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; keratin-deficient yolk cells show reduced actomyosin contraction and decreased pulling forces

title: The four voltage-sensing domains of T-type calcium channels activate near the resting membrane potential
task: Clarify voltage-sensing domain activation mechanism in low-voltage-activated T-type calcium channels
key_results: All four CaV3.1 voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) activate at voltages preceding pore opening, resolving paradox from gating-current studies; CaV3.1-VSDs operate in narrow voltage-range similar to NaV-channels not other CaV-channels
comments: Voltage-clamp fluorometry is superior to traditional gating-current methods and reveals important confounding effects of La3+ used in prior studies.

model_io.model: Human CaV3.1 T-type calcium channel

hypotheses.hypothesis: LVA-channel VSDs require stronger depolarization to activate than pore opening (traditional view)
hypotheses.result: Contradicted; voltage-clamp fluorometry shows VSD activation precedes pore opening in voltage

hypotheses.hypothesis: La3+ has confounding effects on VSD function in gating-current measurements
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; La3+ distorts VSD activation kinetics

hypotheses.hypothesis: CaV3.1-VSDs resemble NaV-channel VSDs more than other CaV-channel VSDs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CaV3.1-VSDs operate in narrow voltage-range characteristic of NaV-channels

title: De novo design of peptides localizing at the interface of biomolecular condensates

comments: Cryo-EM structures elegantly reveal the assembly mechanism, and phylogenetic analysis suggests convergent evolution of this compartmentalization strategy across organisms.

model_io.model: Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis
inputs: LS-RS complex samples at assembly intermediates
outputs: 3D structures of open and closed cages

hypotheses.hypothesis: Delayed cage closure extends enzyme loading window until complete incorporation
